extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of natural philosophy, cosmology, and general theory of evolution
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing and applying a philosophical/scientific theory that unifies changes at all scales as cycles of integration (Evolution) and dispersion (Dissolution), derived from conservation principles. Focuses on laws (persistence of force, continuity of motion) and how they produce structural and functional complexity across astronomical, geological, biological, psychological, and social orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence of Force
rubrics_metrics.description: Force is ultimate and persistent in quantity; from this alone other truths (indestructibility of matter, continuity of motion) are derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the foundational axiom: because force cannot arise from nothing or lapse into nothing, conservation and necessary relations follow. Use this as the primary principle from which laws of co-operation of factors and the law of Evolution are deduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indestructibility of Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter is fixed in quantity (derivable from the persistence of force).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat changes as redistributions of existing matter rather than creation/destruction. Illustrations include planetary and stellar formation and chemical/organic changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of Motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion is fixed in quantity (continuity of motion follows from persistence of force).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kinetic quantities are conserved and transformed; changes in distribution of motion accompany changes in matter (e.g., molecular motion ↔ motion of masses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence of Relations among Forces (Uniformity of Law)
rubrics_metrics.description: The relations among forces persist (uniformity of law) because forces cannot be created or annihilated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This justifies applying the same causal principles throughout nature; use it to expect consistent regularities at all scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformation of Forces (Conservation via Equivalence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forces that seem lost are transformed into equivalent forces; conversely, manifest forces arise by disappearance of pre-existing equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by motions of heavenly bodies, terrestrial changes, organic and super-organic actions. When evaluating a process, account for where 'lost' motion reappears as other forms (e.g., molecular motion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Line of Least Resistance (Resultant Motion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every thing moves along the line of least resistance or the resultant of forces acting on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies from planetary motion to nervous discharges and economic currents; explain observed trajectories and changes by identifying incident forces and their resultant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm of Motion (Alternation)
rubrics_metrics.description: All motion alternates between limits — there is a rhythm of motion, with recurrent reversals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to expect cyclical processes (e.g., evolution ↔ dissolution); rhythm is inevitable given persistence of force and produces long eras of concentration and diffusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Evolution and Dissolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolution: integration (concentration) of matter accompanied by dissipation (loss) of motion. Dissolution: diffusion of matter accompanied by gain (or reappearance) of motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are twin processes that together constitute the whole life-history of aggregates; apply this definition at every scale (stars, planets, organisms, societies, ideas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple vs. Compound Evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple Evolution occurs when an aggregate integrates quickly with rapid dissipation of motion; Compound Evolution arises when integration is slower and secondary redistributions create internal complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the rate of motion dissipation and the aggregate's size/constitution to distinguish simple from compound evolution; compound evolution produces organs, differentiated parts, and functional complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary and Secondary Re-distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary re-distribution: the initial redistribution of matter and motion leading to integration. Secondary re-distributions: concurrent internal rearrangements that produce parts, heterogeneity, and differentiated functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing an evolving system, separate the basic concentration process (primary) from the internal differentiations that yield complexity (secondary); both operate simultaneously and must be united conceptually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progression from Homogeneity to Heterogeneity with Definiteness
rubrics_metrics.description: As aggregation proceeds (diffusion → concentration), systems move from homogeneity to increasing heterogeneity, and parts become more sharply demarcated (definite heterogeneity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Solar System formation, biological organogenesis, societal specialization, language and arts. Expect increasing distinctness of parts as integration advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel Increase in Functional Complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural (material) complexity increases in parallel with functional (motion-related) complexity: arrangement of matter changes along with arrangement of motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret new structural features as accompanied by new movements/functions; e.g., organ formation entails integrated molecular motion into mass motion and diversified movements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication of Effects (Geometric Progression of Heterogeneity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiated parts, by becoming unlike, generate unlike reactions to incident forces and thereby multiply effects; this multiplication advances approximately geometrically with heterogeneity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to explain rapid increases in complexity (geologic complications, organismal symptoms, social ramifications); small initial differences can produce fast-growing complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segregation and Clustering of Similar Units
rubrics_metrics.description: Under forces capable of moving units, mixed units segregate and similar units cluster, producing local integrations that accompany differentiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism explains formation of celestial bodies, crustal segregation, organic differentiation, mental distinctions, and social divisions. Account for mobility of component units when predicting local integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality and Scale-Invariance of Evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: There is one Evolution — the same metamorphosis uniformly progresses at all scales and in all orders (astronomic, geologic, biologic, psychologic, sociologic), not many coincidentally similar processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When theorizing, treat divisions (astronomic, biological, social) as conventional groupings within a single natural whole; apply the same explanatory framework across scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Radiation/Ether in Long-Term Equilibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether aggregated systems can resume original diffusion depends on whether molecular motion radiated into space escapes the system (ether limits); if motion radiates away without compensation, successive cycles may diminish total motion leading to ultimate aggregation or smaller-scale oscillations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For cosmological predictions, consider whether the interstellar medium/ether exchanges motion with the system; if motion is lost to remote space, cycles may trend towards reduced spatial extent or final aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of Whole-History Accounting for Philosophical Unification
rubrics_metrics.description: A philosophy that unifies knowledge must account for the whole history of existences — from imperceptible to perceptible and back — otherwise it is incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses must not begin or stop at existing concrete forms alone; include preceding and succeeding histories (formation and dissolution) to achieve true unification of phenomena.
